clue.text: Not an irreversible mistake

indicators.note: a word that cannot be reversed into something different reads the same both ways, so the clue points to a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone insists a blunder can still be undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not an irreversible' sounds as if the mistake can be put right, but it says the word reads the same backwards and forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal British slang for a silly blunder or error.

clue.text: Barely crowned, he's unaffected by 10

parts.note: a man whose crown is bare has nothing on top to stand on end, so a terrifying experience cannot make his locks rise

explanation.surface: A bald man stays calm in the face of a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is the across entry meaning a terrifying experience; a man with no hair on top cannot have it stand on end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bald pate is a hairless crown of the head, and by extension a man who has one.

clue.text: Regular charge

definitions.meaning: regular in the sense of normal or everyday
in heraldry an ... is a simple geometric charge, such as a bend or chevron, on a shield

explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary means normal or regular, and heraldry calls a basic band or stripe on a shield a charge of this name.

clue.text: Potential queen succeeded pop

parts.note: to pass a test is to succeed in it
to pop something is British slang for pawning it

explanation.surface: A would-be monarch has made it through and burst forth.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess a passed pawn has no enemy pawns blocking its way and may be promoted to a queen. 'Pop' is slang for leaving goods at a pawnshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess pawn with a clear run can reach the last rank and be promoted, making it a queen in waiting.

clue.text: Fine musical instrument needed for dramatic production

indicators.note: the letters needed are a run taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A quality instrument is required for a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona, highly prized by players.

clue.text: Reason for bad reception of person cooking eggs

definitions.meaning: a device that garbles a radio or phone signal
someone who scrambles eggs in a pan

explanation.definitionFit: A device that garbles signals is a cause of poor reception, and a cook beating eggs in a pan does the same job to them.

clue.text: US selectors, we hear, needed to support men in game

indicators.note: we hear says the words are to be judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a draft board is the American body choosing men for military service

explanation.surface: American selectors are wanted to back the players in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAUGHTS is the British name for checkers, and the pieces are called men; a US draft board picks conscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: The checkered board on which the pieces called men are placed during a game of checkers.

clue.text: Appropriate don

definitions.meaning: to appropriate is to take over or seize
to don is to put on, as clothes or a manner

explanation.definitionFit: To assume power is to seize it, and to assume a disguise is to put it on.

clue.text: Country that's certainly not without king

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these words go round the king

parts.note: no way is an emphatic refusal
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A nation that definitely refuses to be ruled by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks as if it means 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside', so the refusal is wrapped round the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian kingdom in northern Europe.

clue.text: Luck, for example, with bet covering first in Derby

indicators.note: covering means the bet wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to lay is to place a bet

indicators.note: first in picks out the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Fortune smiles on a wager at the start of the famous horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's best-known flat horse race, which fits the betting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck is personified as a woman in the phrase Lady Luck, so she is an example of a titled woman.

clue.text: Terrifying experience that heightens level of shock

definitions.meaning: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, and fright makes it stand up higher

explanation.definitionFit: A thriller makes the hair stand on end, so it literally raises the level of a shock of hair.

clue.text: Suitable compositions for house organ?

parts.note: a house organ sounds like a company newsletter, but here it is an instrument played in a room of the house, and the works suited to it are those for small rooms

explanation.surface: Someone asks what pieces would suit a household instrument or newsletter.
explanation.definitionFit: Works written for a small group of players, originally meant for performance in a private room.

clue.text: No belief could be more widespread than this

definitions.text: No belief could be more widespread than this

parts.words: No belief could be more widespread than this
parts.note: a creed that sees the divine in absolutely everything is spread as widely as any belief could be

explanation.surface: A claim that some faith is the most popular in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Widespread' suggests popularity, but the point is that this belief finds God spread through all of nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine identifying God with the whole universe, so its deity is everywhere at once.

clue.text: Poor mark in school got by scholar

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A pupil gets a low grade at school from a learned examiner.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamma, the third Greek letter, is a low grade in some British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: In British university marking schemes using Greek letters, the third grade is a weak result.

clue.text: In which every other part is a Greek dish

definitions.text: In which every other part is a Greek dish

parts.words: In which every other part is a Greek dish
parts.note: read literally, every second letter of the dish's name is an A, as the words every other part is a say

explanation.surface: A dish in which alternate ingredients are Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's second, fourth, sixth and every following even letter is A, so 'every other part is a' is a literal description.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek dip made from fish roe, bread or potato, oil and lemon.

clue.text: One's not prepared to perform musically like this

definitions.text: One's not prepared to perform musically like this

parts.words: One's not prepared to perform musically like this
parts.note: a musician who plays an unfamiliar score at first glance, without rehearsal, performs unprepared

explanation.surface: A performer admits to being unready for a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: To play or sing music at first sight of the score, without any practice beforehand.

clue.text: Poet of the sea, given recital in French

indicators.note: a recital is a speaking aloud, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: de la mer is French for of the sea

explanation.surface: A maritime poet whose work is read out in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French' tells the solver to translate 'of the sea' into French. Walter de la Mare was an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet and writer of children's verse.

clue.text: Medical record compiled by doctor for famous consultant

definitions.text: compiled by doctor for famous consultant
definitions.meaning: Dr Arthur Conan Doyle compiled The ... of Sherlock Holmes, the famous consulting detective

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's file of patients, and also the title of Conan Doyle's last collection of detective stories.

clue.text: Rich production that inspired Weill's low-budget version?

definitions.text: Rich production that inspired Weill's low-budget version?

parts.words: Rich production that inspired Weill's low-budget version?
parts.note: John Rich staged Gay's ballad opera in 1728, and Kurt Weill's reworking is called The Threepenny Opera, hence low-budget

explanation.surface: A lavish show inspired a cheap copy by a German composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like 'lavish', but John Rich was the theatre manager who first produced the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's 1728 ballad opera, which Brecht and Weill adapted as The Threepenny Opera.

clue.text: So woman may be' dubbed authoress and artist

parts.note: George Sand was a French woman novelist
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A woman is nicknamed after a writer and a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Make 'scores of forty, for example

parts.note: split forty into two equal parts and each is a score, so turning forty into scores is halving it

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to make high totals in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so dividing forty into scores means cutting it in two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something into two equal parts.

clue.text: Man, after a vote, accepted proposition

indicators.note: after places the island's letters following the other pieces

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man, having voted, agrees to a suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement taken as self-evidently true without proof.

clue.text: He conquered a huge' area in relatively gentle way

parts.note: tamer is the comparative of tame
a lane is a narrow road or way

explanation.surface: A conqueror swept across a vast region more mildly than others.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamerlane, or Timur, was a 14th-century Central Asian conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: Timur, the Turco-Mongol warlord known in English as Tamburlaine, built an empire across Asia.

clue.text: Stone-carver's" "Mother' and Child"

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A sculptor's work titled Mother and Child.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the surface a title of a carving.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who cuts and dresses stone.

clue.text: It's used to select the appropriate gear

definitions.text: It's used to select the appropriate gear

parts.words: It's used to select the appropriate gear
parts.note: gear means clothing, and the faculty for choosing the right outfit is meant, not a gearbox

explanation.surface: A gear lever in a car picks the right ratio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests a car's gearbox; it is informal for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct for choosing clothes that suit the wearer and the occasion.

clue.text: Initial pronouncement that ends a fight

definitions.text: Initial pronouncement that ends a fight

parts.words: Initial pronouncement that ends a fight
parts.note: the initials of a boxing knockout, spoken as two letters, give the slang word

explanation.surface: An opening announcement brings a bout to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial' looks like 'first', but it means the initials K and O, spelt out as they sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing slang for a knockout, formed from saying its abbreviation.

clue.text: Prior having bet with church to make an impression

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
CE is the Church of England
a dent is an impression left in a surface

explanation.surface: A monastic superior gambles alongside the church to impress people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a monastic title, but it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Antecedent means coming before in time or order.

clue.text: Summit providing view —- but not for long, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is to be judged by how it sounds spoken

parts.note: a peek is a brief look, a view that does not last

explanation.surface: A mountaintop offers a fleeting glimpse of the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the pointed top of a mountain.
